questions.question: Define technology and give an example of technology used in each of the three sectors.
questions.expected_answer: Technology is the application of knowledge and skills to create tools, machines and methods for producing goods and services. Primary e.g. GPS tractors, drip irrigation, mining drills. Secondary e.g. robots on car assembly lines, computer-controlled cutters. Tertiary e.g. barcode scanners, online banking, computers in schools.

questions.question: Distinguish between labour-intensive and capital-intensive production with an example of each, and explain why labour-intensive industries matter in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Labour-intensive: many workers relative to machines, e.g. fruit picking, crafts, hairdressing, public works road building. Capital-intensive: many machines relative to workers, e.g. automated car plant, bottling plant, oil refinery. SA has very high unemployment, so labour-intensive industries absorb many workers, especially those with fewer skills.

questions.question: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of technology in production, and two skills young people need.
questions.expected_answer: Advantages (any two): higher productivity; lower cost per unit; better quality; safer work; new products and markets; less waste. Disadvantages (any two): some jobs replaced; high cost; needs reliable electricity/internet; training needed; may widen inequality; privacy concerns. Skills (any two): maths, science, reading; digital skills; problem-solving and creativity; communication and teamwork; technical/vocational skills; lifelong learning.
